page: Microsoft Azure D248ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, powered by Intel x86_64 processors. Designed for massive enterprise applications requiring substantial compute and memory balance, the instance provides 248 dedicated vCPUs and 992.0 GB of RAM. This maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include hardware GPU acceleration.

A key differentiator for this server type is its bundled high-capacity local storage subsystem. The configuration includes 15,118 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage, alongside support for Premium Storage remote disk caching. This extensive local NVMe disk array provides low-latency temporary scratch space without incurring independent external storage transfer overheads, though data on ephemeral disks does not persist across virtual machine deallocations.

From an architectural standpoint, the D248ds_v7 delivers high resource density within a single guest operating system. Organizations utilizing this footprint benefit from consolidated operational overhead, reducing multi-node clustering complexity for workloads that scale vertically. The absence of public IPv4 addresses standardizes deployments within private virtual networks.

This server type is suitable for large-scale enterprise databases, intensive transactional systems, big data processing engines, distributed build pipelines, and high-density application hosting layers requiring substantial temporary NVMe scratch capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure D248ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Intel-based Ddsv7 family, architected for high-density compute and memory requirements. It features 248 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 992.0 GB of system memory, providing a consistent 1:4 allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates 15,118 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage extensions, ensuring extensive low-latency local disk throughput for scratch space and temporary file operations. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization without GPU accelerators, it provides massive single-node scale. This profile reduces coordination overhead inherent in distributed architectures, making the D248ds_v7 well suited for heavy enterprise databases, large-scale continuous integration platforms, in-memory processing pipelines, and data analytics tasks requiring dense CPU capacity alongside vast ephemeral NVMe storage.
